claim: Single-molecule FRET (smFRET) has become a mainstream technique for studying biomolecular structural dynamics.
source: Single-molecule FRET (smFRET) has become a mainstream technique for studying biomolecular structural dynamics.
evidence: This statement is directly made in the abstract and reflects the current state of the field as described by the authors.

claim: Several labs that employ smFRET approaches have joined forces to inform the smFRET community about streamlining how to perform experiments and analyze results for obtaining quantitative information on biomolecular structure and dynamics.
source: Several labs that employ smFRET approaches have joined forces to inform the smFRET community about streamlining how to perform experiments and analyze results for obtaining quantitative information on biomolecular structure and dynamics.
evidence: This is a factual statement about collaborative efforts within the smFRET community as described in the abstract.

claim: Recent efforts include blind tests to assess the accuracy and the precision of smFRET experiments among different labs using various procedures.
source: The recent efforts include blind tests to assess the accuracy and the precision of smFRET experiments among different labs using various procedures.
evidence: This statement describes specific activities undertaken by the community as mentioned in the abstract.

claim: Multi-lab studies have led to the development of smFRET procedures and documentation, which are important when submitting entries into the archiving system for integrative structure models, PDB-Dev.
source: These multi-lab studies have led to the development of smFRET procedures and documentation, which are important when submitting entries into the archiving system for integrative structure models, PDB-Dev.
evidence: This claim describes outcomes of collaborative efforts and their relevance to data archiving.

claim: Understanding how biomolecules couple structural dynamics with function is at the heart of several disciplines and remains an outstanding goal in biology.
source: Understanding how biomolecules couple structural dynamics with function is at the heart of several disciplines and remains an outstanding goal in biology.
evidence: This is a statement about the fundamental importance of the research area.

claim: The most well-established structural biology tools have provided high-resolution 'snapshots' of states in a crystallized or frozen form (e.g., X-ray crystallography and single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, cryoEM) or an ensemble average of all contributing conformations (e.g., nuclear magnetic resonance, NMR; small-angle X-ray scattering, SAXS; small-angle neutron scattering, SANS; double electron-electron resonance, DEER; cross-linking mass spectrometry, XL-MS; ensemble-FRET).
source: The most well-established structural biology tools have provided high-resolution 'snapshots' of states in a crystallized or frozen form (e.g., X-ray crystallography and single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, cryoEM) or an ensemble average of all contributing conformations (e.g., nuclear magnetic resonance, NMR; small-angle X-ray scattering, SAXS; small-angle neutron scattering, SANS; double electron-electron resonance, DEER; cross-linking mass spectrometry, XL-MS; ensemble-FRET).
evidence: This statement describes the capabilities of established structural biology methods.

claim: NMR techniques have been advanced to study conformational dynamics and capture transient intermediates.
source: For example, NMR techniques (Anthis and Clore, 2015; Clore and Iwahara, 2009; Palmer, 2004; Ravera et al., 2014; Sekhar and Kay, 2019) and electron paramagnetic resonance techniques (Jeschke, 2018; Jeschke, 2012; Krstić et al., 2011) have been advanced to study conformational dynamics and capture transient intermediates.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Electron paramagnetic resonance techniques have been advanced to study conformational dynamics and capture transient intermediates.
source: For example, NMR techniques (Anthis and Clore, 2015; Clore and Iwahara, 2009; Palmer, 2004; Ravera et al., 2014; Sekhar and Kay, 2019) and electron paramagnetic resonance techniques (Jeschke, 2018; Jeschke, 2012; Krstić et al., 2011) have been advanced to study conformational dynamics and capture transient intermediates.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Time-resolved crystallographic investigations have been employed to resolve functionally relevant structural displacements associated with a biological function.
source: Time-resolved crystallographic investigations have been employed to resolve functionally relevant structural displacements associated with a biological function (Kupitz et al., 2014; Moffat, 2001; Schlichting et al., 1990; Schlichting and Chu, 2000; Schotte et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Advances in microfluidic mixing and spraying devices have enabled time-resolved cryoEM.
source: Advances in microfluidic mixing and spraying devices have enabled time-resolved cryoEM (Feng et al., 2017; Kaledhonkar et al., 2018) and cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS or CL-MS) (Braitbard et al., 2019; Brodie et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2020; Iacobucci et al., 2019; Murakami et al., 2013; Slavin and Kalisman, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Advances in microfluidic mixing and spraying devices have enabled cross-linking mass spectrometry.
source: Advances in microfluidic mixing and spraying devices have enabled time-resolved cryoEM (Feng et al., 2017; Kaledhonkar et al., 2018) and cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS or CL-MS) (Braitbard et al., 2019; Brodie et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2020; Iacobucci et al., 2019; Murakami et al., 2013; Slavin and Kalisman, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: FRET studies at the ensemble and single-molecule levels have emerged as important tools for measuring structural dynamics over at least 12 orders of magnitude in time and mapping the conformational and functional heterogeneities of biomolecules under ambient conditions.
source: In this context, FRET (referred to as fluorescence resonance energy transfer or Förster resonance energy transfer [Braslavsky et al., 2008]) studies at the ensemble and single-molecule levels have emerged as important tools for measuring structural dynamics over at least 12 orders of magnitude in time and mapping the conformational and functional heterogeneities of biomolecules under ambient conditions.
evidence: This statement describes the capabilities of FRET techniques.

claim: FRET studies probing fluorescence decays at the ensemble level (time-resolved FRET) permitted already in the early 1970s the study of structural heterogeneities on timescales longer than the fluorescence lifetime (a few ns).
source: FRET studies probing fluorescence decays at the ensemble level (Grinvald et al., 1972; Haas et al., 1975; Haas and Steinberg, 1984; Hochstrasser et al., 1992) (time-resolved FRET) permitted already in the early 1970s the study of structural heterogeneities on timescales longer than the fluorescence lifetime (a few ns).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to historical work in the field.

claim: The ability to measure FRET in single molecules has made the method even more appealing.
source: The ability to measure FRET in single molecules (Deniz et al., 1999; Ha et al., 1996; Lerner et al., 2018a) has made the method even more appealing.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to foundational smFRET work.

claim: The single-molecule FRET (smFRET) approach has been extensively used to study conformational dynamics and biomolecular interactions under steady-state conditions.
source: The single-molecule FRET (smFRET) approach has been extensively used to study conformational dynamics and biomolecular interactions under steady-state conditions (Dupuis et al., 2014; Larsen et al., 2019; Lerner et al., 2018a; Lipman et al., 2003; Margittai et al., 2003; Mazal and Haran, 2019; Michalet et al., 2006; Orevi et al., 2014; Ray et al., 2019; Sasmal et al., 2016; Schuler et al., 2005; Schuler et al., 2002; Steiner et al., 2008; Zhuang et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by numerous citations to published work.

claim: In many mechanistic studies, it suffices to use FRET for distinguishing different conformations and determining kinetic rates such that absolute FRET efficiencies and thereby distances do not need to be determined.
source: It is notable that, in many mechanistic studies, it suffices to use FRET for distinguishing different conformations and determining kinetic rates such that absolute FRET efficiencies and thereby distances do not need to be determined.
evidence: This statement describes a common practice in the field.

claim: The ability to measure accurate distances and kinetics with smFRET has led to its emergence as an important tool in this new era of 'dynamic structural biology' for mapping biomolecular heterogeneities and for measuring structural dynamics over a wide range of timescales.
source: However, the ability to measure accurate distances and kinetics with smFRET has led to its emergence as an important tool in this new era of 'dynamic structural biology' for mapping biomolecular heterogeneities and for measuring structural dynamics over a wide range of timescales (Lerner et al., 2018a; Mazal and Haran, 2019; Sanabria et al., 2020; Schuler and Hofmann, 2013; Weiss, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Several methods have been utilized to determine structural ensembles such as NMR, single-particle cryoEM or XL-MS, and, recently, also smFRET in an integrative/hybrid (I/H) approach with computational modeling to overcome the sparsity of experimental data with respect to an atomistic description.
source: Several methods have been utilized to determine structural ensembles such as NMR, single-particle cryoEM or XL-MS, and, recently, also smFRET in an integrative/hybrid (I/H) approach with computational modeling to overcome the sparsity of experimental data with respect to an atomistic description (Berman et al., 2019; de Souza and Picotti, 2020; Dimura et al., 2020; Gauto et al., 2019; Koukos and Bonvin, 2020; Na and Paek, 2020; Tang and Gong, 2020; Webb et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: I/H structural models derived from smFRET experiments using inter-dye distances as restraints were reported for flexible folded proteins.
source: I/H structural models derived from smFRET experiments using inter-dye distances as restraints were reported for flexible folded proteins (Brunger et al., 2011; Hellenkamp et al., 2017; Margittai et al., 2003; McCann et al., 2012), conformational ensembles of disordered/unstructured and unfolded proteins (Borgia et al., 2018; Holmstrom et al., 2018; Schuler et al., 2020), nucleic acids and protein-nucleic acid complexes (Craggs et al., 2019; Craggs and Kapanidis, 2012; Kalinin et al., 2012; Lerner et al., 2018b; Muschielok et al., 2008; Wozniak et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: I/H structural models derived from smFRET experiments using inter-dye distances as restraints were reported for conformational ensembles of disordered/unstructured and unfolded proteins.
source: I/H structural models derived from smFRET experiments using inter-dye distances as restraints were reported for flexible folded proteins (Brunger et al., 2011; Hellenkamp et al., 2017; Margittai et al., 2003; McCann et al., 2012), conformational ensembles of disordered/unstructured and unfolded proteins (Borgia et al., 2018; Holmstrom et al., 2018; Schuler et al., 2020), nucleic acids and protein-nucleic acid complexes (Craggs et al., 2019; Craggs and Kapanidis, 2012; Kalinin et al., 2012; Lerner et al., 2018b; Muschielok et al., 2008; Wozniak et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: I/H structural models derived from smFRET experiments using inter-dye distances as restraints were reported for nucleic acids and protein-nucleic acid complexes.
source: I/H structural models derived from smFRET experiments using inter-dye distances as restraints were reported for flexible folded proteins (Brunger et al., 2011; Hellenkamp et al., 2017; Margittai et al., 2003; McCann et al., 2012), conformational ensembles of disordered/unstructured and unfolded proteins (Borgia et al., 2018; Holmstrom et al., 2018; Schuler et al., 2020), nucleic acids and protein-nucleic acid complexes (Craggs et al., 2019; Craggs and Kapanidis, 2012; Kalinin et al., 2012; Lerner et al., 2018b; Muschielok et al., 2008; Wozniak et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: A multimodal smFRET study on the conformational landscape of a 12-mer chromatin array (~2.5 MDa) detected flexible chromatin conformations with dynamics occurring on timescales from nanoseconds to hours.
source: As an example, Figure 1B shows the outcome of a multimodal smFRET study on the conformational landscape of a 12-mer chromatin array (~2.5 MDa) (Kilic et al., 2018) with dynamics occurring on timescales from nanoseconds to hours.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and reference to Figure 1B showing experimental data.

claim: SmFRET experiments on chromatin fibers revealed flexible, partially-open and open conformations that are quite abundant in solution (population of >70%).
source: SmFRET experiments could detect the flexible chromatin conformations (Figure 1B, middle panel), revealing their dynamic structural heterogeneity (Figure 1B, bottom panel), in contrast to the well-ordered static structures of chromatin fibers (Figure 1B, top panel). These flexible, partially-open and open conformations that are quite abundant in solution (population of >70%; Figure 1B, bottom panel) were not resolved before, although they are essential for proper gene organization and function.
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1B showing experimental data.

claim: Twenty laboratories joined in measuring smFRET on several dsDNA constructs to assess reproducibility.
source: To this end, in an effort led by Thorsten Hugel, twenty laboratories joined in measuring smFRET on several dsDNA constructs (Hellenkamp et al., 2018a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published multi-lab study.

claim: The quantitative assessment and reproducibility of the intensity-based smFRET measurements and discussions about data analysis was an important milestone.
source: The quantitative assessment and reproducibility of the intensity-based smFRET measurements and discussions about data analysis was an important milestone.
evidence: This is an evaluative statement about the significance of the multi-lab study.

claim: dsDNA FRET standards are now available for every day calibration and are especially useful for new groups joining the community.
source: These dsDNA FRET standards are now available for every day calibration and are especially useful for new groups joining the community.
evidence: This statement describes the availability and utility of reference materials.

claim: A new multi-lab blind study investigates the robustness and reliability of smFRET experiments on proteins undergoing ligand-induced conformational changes.
source: The next comparative FRET study, led by Thorben Cordes, investigates the robustness and reliability of smFRET experiments on proteins undergoing ligand-induced conformational changes (Gebhardt et al., in preparation).
evidence: This claim describes an ongoing study.

claim: The protein-based smFRET study uses two distinct model proteins to assess the reproducibility and accuracy of protein-based smFRET for inter-dye distance determination measurements.
source: This study uses two distinct model proteins to assess the reproducibility and accuracy of protein-based smFRET for inter-dye distance determination measurements.
evidence: This claim describes the design of an ongoing study.

claim: The protein-based smFRET study assesses the ability of smFRET to discover and quantify dynamics on different timescales from microseconds to seconds.
source: Hence, the study also assesses the ability of smFRET to discover and quantify dynamics on different timescales from microseconds to seconds.
evidence: This claim describes the objectives of an ongoing study.

claim: The kinSoftChallenge evaluates existing tools for extracting kinetic information from single-molecule time trajectories.
source: Another FRET challenge, initiated by Sonja Schmid, is the kinSoftChallenge (http://www.kinsoftchallenge.com, Götz et al., in preparation), which evaluates existing tools for extracting kinetic information from single-molecule time trajectories.
evidence: This claim describes an ongoing community challenge.

claim: Although the agreement in the multi-lab FRET studies was good, it could be improved even further.
source: One important outcome of the various multi-lab FRET studies was that, although the agreement was good, it could be improved even further.
evidence: This is an evaluative statement about the results of multi-lab studies.

claim: The data analysis, and specifically corrections, can have an impact on the determined FRET efficiencies and resulting distances.
source: In particular, the data analysis, and specifically corrections, can have an impact on the determined FRET efficiencies and resulting distances.
evidence: This statement describes a methodological consideration in smFRET analysis.

claim: Access to the primary data and the ability to process them with various analysis approaches is the most transparent way to move the field forward.
source: Access to the primary data and the ability to process them with various analysis approaches is, and will remain, the most transparent way to move the field forward.
evidence: This is a recommendation about open science practices.

claim: SmFRET measurements are typically performed using two approaches: with surface-immobilized molecules using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy (TIRFM) and camera-based detection, or with freely diffusing molecules in solution using confocal microscopy and point detectors.
source: SmFRET measurements are typically performed using two approaches: with surface-immobilized molecules using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy (TIRFM) and camera-based detection, or with freely diffusing molecules in solution using confocal microscopy and point detectors.
evidence: This statement describes the two main experimental modalities in smFRET.

claim: Confocal microscopy is especially well-suited for studying freely diffusing molecules.
source: Confocal microscopy is especially well-suited for studying freely diffusing molecules (Figure 2A), while TIRF microscopy is typically used for surface-immobilized molecules (Figure 2B; e.g., reviewed in Juette et al., 2014; Roy et al., 2008; Sasmal et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and reference to Figure 2.

claim: TIRF microscopy is typically used for surface-immobilized molecules.
source: Confocal microscopy is especially well-suited for studying freely diffusing molecules (Figure 2A), while TIRF microscopy is typically used for surface-immobilized molecules (Figure 2B; e.g., reviewed in Juette et al., 2014; Roy et al., 2008; Sasmal et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and reference to Figure 2.

claim: Compared to most other single-molecule approaches, both smFRET modalities offer relatively high throughput.
source: Compared to most other single-molecule approaches, both smFRET modalities offer relatively high throughput.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about the capabilities of smFRET methods.

claim: The dynamical aspects of the biological system under investigation will eventually define which of the two methods (confocal or TIRF) is best suited.
source: However, the dynamical aspects (reviewed in section Conformational dynamics) of the biological system under investigation, which are typically not known a priori, will eventually define which of the two methods is best suited.
evidence: This statement describes how method selection depends on the system being studied.

claim: Biomolecular dynamics occur over a range of timescales from nanoseconds to seconds.
source: Because the dynamics of biological systems occur over a range of timescales from nanoseconds to seconds (Figure 3), ideally one would like to apply both modalities in parallel to obtain a complete understanding of the system (e.g., as shown in Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3 showing the timescale range.

claim: For studying biomolecular conformations and their dynamics with smFRET, the biomolecules of interest must be labeled with organic dyes that are suitable for single-molecule fluorescence detection.
source: For studying biomolecular conformations and their dynamics with smFRET, the biomolecules of interest must be labeled with organic dyes that are suitable for single-molecule fluorescence detection (intrinsically fluorescent aromatic amino acids are not stable or bright enough).
evidence: This statement describes a fundamental requirement for smFRET experiments.

claim: Intrinsically fluorescent aromatic amino acids are not stable or bright enough for single-molecule fluorescence detection.
source: For studying biomolecular conformations and their dynamics with smFRET, the biomolecules of interest must be labeled with organic dyes that are suitable for single-molecule fluorescence detection (intrinsically fluorescent aromatic amino acids are not stable or bright enough).
evidence: This statement explains why extrinsic labels are necessary.

claim: The fluorescence lifetime of smFRET-compatible dyes should be on the 1-5 ns scale.
source: The fluorescence lifetime should be on the 1-5 ns scale.
evidence: This statement provides a technical requirement for dyes used in smFRET.

claim: For TCSPC experiments, a general rule of thumb is that the laser repetition period should be chosen at least four times as large as the fluorescence lifetime.
source: In the case of TCSPC experiments, a general rule of thumb is that the laser repetition period should be chosen at least four times as large as the fluorescence lifetime.
evidence: This statement provides a guideline for experimental setup.

claim: Site-specific conjugations in proteins utilize the introduction of point mutations, typically to cysteines, that will accommodate the specific conjugation chemistry, usually maleimide- or iodoacetamide-cysteine chemistry.
source: Site-specific conjugations in proteins utilize the introduction of point mutations, typically to cysteines, that will accommodate the specific conjugation chemistry, usually maleimide- or iodoacetamide-cysteine chemistry.
evidence: This statement describes a common labeling strategy for proteins.

claim: Two cysteines are often stochastically labeled, leading to a mixture of donor-acceptor and acceptor-donor labeled molecules.
source: In this case, two cysteines are often stochastically labeled, leading to a mixture of donor-acceptor and acceptor-donor labeled molecules.
evidence: This statement describes a consequence of stochastic labeling.

claim: Interchanging the donor and acceptor positions has a negligible effect, from the geometric standpoint, on the FRET-averaged distance.
source: While interchanging the donor and acceptor positions has a negligible effect, from the geometric standpoint, on the FRET-averaged distance (Peulen et al., 2017), stochastic labeling might cause problems when the donor/acceptor dyes possess different spectroscopic properties at the different labeling positions.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: For short nucleic acids, site-specific conjugation is generally achieved by post-synthetic labeling of reactive groups (e.g., through click chemistry) that are incorporated during solid-phase synthesis.
source: For short nucleic acids, site-specific conjugation is generally achieved by post-synthetic labeling of reactive groups (e.g., through click chemistry) that are incorporated during solid-phase synthesis.
evidence: This statement describes a common labeling strategy for nucleic acids.

claim: Strategies have been developed to site-specifically label longer RNAs.
source: Strategies have also been developed to site-specifically label longer RNAs (Anhäuser and Rentmeister, 2017; Baum and Silverman, 2007; Büttner et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2018), and the use of hybridizing probes (Steiner et al., 2008) and fluorescent nucleobase analogues as intrinsic probes (Karimi et al., 2020; Steinmetzger et al., 2020) has been explored.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: A general recommendation for labeling is to aim for high-purity sample preparations with optimized labeling protocols, as only this will result in substantially and specifically labeled samples with both donor and acceptor dyes.
source: A general recommendation for labeling is to aim for high-purity sample preparations with optimized labeling protocols, as only this will result in substantially and specifically labeled samples with both donor and acceptor dyes.
evidence: This is a recommendation for sample preparation.

claim: After labeling, a rigorous screening procedure should be used that compares the activities of labeled and unlabeled wild-type biomolecules to determine whether the mutations introduced to a biomolecule and/or the labeling with the dyes significantly influence the biomolecule's functionality and stability.
source: After labeling, we recommend using a rigorous screening procedure that compares the activities of labeled and unlabeled wild-type biomolecules to determine whether the mutations introduced to a biomolecule and/or the labeling with the dyes significantly influence the biomolecule's functionality (e.g., catalytic activity, binding affinity) and stability (e.g., against denaturants or thermally-induced transition curves) (Best et al., 2018; Deniz et al., 2000; Lerner et al., 2018b; Orevi et al., 2014; Riback et al., 2019; Sottini et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a recommendation supported by citations to published work.

claim: For long observation times, labeled molecules are typically immobilized via a biotin-streptavidin linkage.
source: For long observation times, labeled molecules are typically immobilized. This is most frequently achieved via a biotin-streptavidin linkage.
evidence: This statement describes a common immobilization strategy.

claim: Immobilization must be carefully performed in order to systematically eliminate spurious contributions from molecules that are non-specifically bound.
source: Immobilization must be carefully performed in order to systematically eliminate spurious contributions from molecules that are non-specifically bound (Lamichhane et al., 2010; Traeger and Schwartz, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Efforts have been made to optimize surface passivation procedures.
source: To address this potential issue, efforts have been made to optimize surface passivation procedures (Hua et al., 2014; Kuzmenkina et al., 2005; Park et al., 2020; Selvin and Ha, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Fluorescent dyes are characterized by particular spectroscopic properties, which may change when conjugated to a protein.
source: Fluorescent dyes are characterized by particular spectroscopic properties, which may change when conjugated to a protein (Lerner et al., 2013; Peulen et al., 2017; Sindbert et al., 2011; Steffen et al., 2016) or even between different structural states of the labeled biomolecule (Kudryavtsev et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: When the local and/or global environment influences the photophysical properties of either the donor or the acceptor dyes differently, different subpopulations might appear.
source: When the local and/or global environment influences the photophysical properties of either the donor or the acceptor dyes differently, different subpopulations might appear (Kalinin et al., 2010a; Vandenberk et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Chemical photostabilizers are often added to reduce oxidative photodamage by lowering the time spent in triplet or radical-ion dark states.
source: Often, chemical photostabilizers are added to reduce oxidative photodamage by lowering the time spent in triplet or radical-ion dark states (Ha and Tinnefeld, 2012; Widengren et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Commonly used photostabilizers for smFRET include Trolox, n-propylgallate, β-mercaptoethanol, ascorbic acid, linear polyenes, cyclopolyenes, and methylviologen.
source: Commonly used photostabilizers for smFRET include 6-hydroxy-2,5,7,8-tetramethylchroman-2-carboxylic acid (Trolox) (Cordes et al., 2009; Dave et al., 2009; Rasnik et al., 2006; Vandenberk et al., 2018), n-propylgallate (Widengren et al., 2007), β-mercaptoethanol (Campos et al., 2011; Ha and Tinnefeld, 2012), ascorbic acid (Aitken et al., 2008; Gidi et al., 2020; Vogelsang et al., 2008; Widengren et al., 2007), linear polyenes (Pfiffi et al., 2010) and cyclopolyenes (Dave et al., 2009; Targowski et al., 1987; Widengren et al., 2007), methylviologen (Vogelsang et al., 2008) and a range of other compounds (Glembockyte et al., 2015; Isselstein et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: In the confocal modality, the raw 'burst' data includes a sequence of photon detection or arrival times from at least two detectors.
source: In the confocal modality, the raw 'burst' data includes a sequence of photon detection or arrival times from at least two detectors.
evidence: This statement describes the nature of confocal data.

claim: Various approaches have been described for the robust and accurate detection of single-molecule events (burst search).
source: Various approaches have been described for the robust and accurate detection of single-molecule events (Enderlein et al., 1997; Fries et al., 1998; Nir et al., 2006; Schaffer et al., 1999; Sisamakis et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: The burst search and burst selection criteria have an impact on the resulting smFRET histograms.
source: The burst search and burst selection criteria have an impact on the resulting smFRET histograms.
evidence: This statement describes a methodological consideration.

claim: Molecule sorting algorithms in the confocal modality, such as those based on ALEX/PIE, do not suffer from a substantial user bias.
source: Despite the ability to manually determine burst search and selection criteria, molecule sorting algorithms in the confocal modality, such as those based on ALEX/PIE (Kapanidis et al., 2005; Kudryavtsev et al., 2012; Tomov et al., 2012), do not suffer from a substantial user bias.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: In the early days, many TIRF modality users have relied on visual inspection of individual single-molecule traces.
source: In the early days, many TIRF modality users have relied on visual inspection of individual single-molecule traces.
evidence: This statement describes historical practices in the field.

claim: User bias in TIRF analysis was considerably reduced by the use of hard selection criteria, such as intensity-based thresholds and single-step photobleaching, intensity-based automatic sorting algorithms, and artificial intelligence-based molecular sorting.
source: Such user bias was considerably reduced by the use of hard selection criteria, such as intensity-based thresholds and single-step photobleaching, intensity-based automatic sorting algorithms (e.g., as implemented in the programs MASH-FRET [Hadzic et al., 2019], iSMS [Preus et al., 2015] or SPARTAN [Juette et al., 2016]), and, most recently, artificial intelligence-based molecular sorting (deepFRET [Thomsen et al., 2020] and AutoSiM [Li et al., 2020a]).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Many users in the FRET community employ the detection and characterization of different subpopulations or measurements of conformational dynamics as a handle to study biomolecules or biomolecular systems.
source: Many users in the FRET community employ the detection and characterization of different subpopulations or measurements of conformational dynamics as a handle to study biomolecules or biomolecular systems.
evidence: This statement describes common practices in the field.

claim: SmFRET is unique in that it allows the detection and analysis of equilibrium and non-equilibrium conformational dynamics across at least 12 orders of magnitude in time, that is from the nanoseconds to, in principle, thousands of seconds.
source: SmFRET is unique in that it allows the detection and analysis of equilibrium and non-equilibrium conformational dynamics across at least 12 orders of magnitude in time, that is from the nanoseconds to, in principle, thousands of seconds (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3.

claim: Biomolecules are dynamic systems that show conformational flexibility and dynamics on fast time scales.
source: Biomolecules are dynamic systems that show conformational flexibility and dynamics on fast time scales (Henzler-Wildman and Kern, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Conformational interconversions often occur on a timescale faster than the sampling time of the detection system, resulting in the observed single-molecule time series or FRET efficiency histogram exhibiting only time-averaged FRET values.
source: Oftentimes, conformational interconversions occur on a timescale faster than the sampling time of the detection system, for example < 10 ms for TIRF modality or < 0.1 ms for confocal modality, resulting in the observed single-molecule time series or FRET efficiency histogram exhibiting only time-averaged FRET values, weighted by the fractional population of each conformational state.
evidence: This statement describes a phenomenon in smFRET measurements.

claim: Several groups have developed methods for detecting and analyzing 'dynamic averaging' from confocal-modality data.
source: Several groups have developed methods for detecting and analyzing such 'dynamic averaging' from confocal-modality data.
evidence: This statement describes methodological developments in the field.

claim: The precise knowledge of the experimental shot noise separates smFRET from other techniques in structural biology and enables a quantitative analysis of fluctuations caused by biomolecular dynamics.
source: The precise knowledge of the experimental shot noise separates smFRET from other techniques in structural biology and enables a quantitative analysis of fluctuations caused by biomolecular dynamics.
evidence: This statement describes a unique advantage of smFRET.

claim: For dynamics on the order of 10 ms or slower, transitions between conformational states can be directly observed using TIRF-modality approaches.
source: For dynamics on the order of 10 ms or slower, transitions between conformational states can be directly observed using TIRF-modality approaches, as have been demonstrated in numerous studies (Blanchard et al., 2004; Deniz, 2016; Juette et al., 2014; Robb et al., 2019; Sasmal et al., 2016; Zhuang et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Hidden Markov models (HMM) are routinely used for a quantitative analysis of smFRET time traces to determine the number of states, the connectivity between them and the individual transition rates.
source: Nowadays, hidden Markov models (HMM) (Figure 4E) are routinely used for a quantitative analysis of smFRET time traces to determine the number of states, the connectivity between them and the individual transition rates (Andrec et al., 2003; Keller et al., 2014; McKinney et al., 2006; Munro et al., 2007; Steffen et al., 2020; Stella et al., 2018; Zarrabi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work and reference to Figure 4E.

claim: For many smFRET studies, a qualitative indicator of the inter-probe distance is sufficient, for example, to merely be able to distinguish between conformational subpopulations or their transitions.

claim: The γ factor is identified as the major contribution to uncertainty in smFRET experiments.
source: The optimal procedures for determining the correction parameters is still a matter of active debate within the community. In the following, we focus on the γ factor, which we identify as the major contribution to uncertainty in smFRET experiments.
evidence: This is an assessment of sources of uncertainty in smFRET.

claim: The uncertainty in the determination of γ is one of the largest contributions to discrepancies of smFRET histograms measured from different laboratories.

claim: The advantage of the lifetime approach is that correction factors are not needed, as most of the corrections influence the relative number of photons detected in the donor and acceptor channels, but not the donor fluorescence decay.

evidence: This statement describes an advantage of lifetime-based FRET measurements.

claim: In FRET, the excitation energy of the donor fluorophore is transferred to an acceptor fluorophore via weak dipolar coupling.
source: In FRET, the excitation energy of the donor fluorophore is transferred to an acceptor fluorophore via weak dipolar coupling.

claim: The dye transition dipole orientation factor κ2 describes the relative orientation of the transition dipole moments of the dyes and strongly depends on dye mobility.

claim: Since the dyes' orientations can change randomly on the time scale of typical FRET events, the mean value of <κ2> = 2/3 is typically taken.

evidence: This statement describes a common assumption in FRET analysis.

claim: Various groups have developed detailed dye models that account for the translational and rotational flexibility of the dyes and thus allow a more accurate description of the actual distance FRET measures.
source: Various groups have developed detailed dye models that account for the translational and rotational flexibility of the dyes and thus allow a more accurate description of the actual distance FRET measures (Figure 5D) (Beckers et al., 2015; Craggs and Kapanidis, 2012; Dimura et al., 2016; Haas et al., 1978; Kalinin et al., 2012; Muschielok et al., 2008; Schuler et al., 2020; Sindbert et al., 2011) and to test them experimentally (Hellenkamp et al., 2018a; Nagy et al., 2018; Peulen et al., 2017; Wozniak et al., 2008).

claim: The FRET information alone is insufficient to generate an atomistic model de novo.

claim: FRET restraints yielded structural models that showed excellent agreement with existing models in benchmark studies.
